chunks: And Ibrāhīm ibn Sahl ibn Hāshim narrated, saying:

I was with Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام when Ṣāliḥ ibn Muḥammad ibn Sahl entered upon him, and he used to administer the endowment for him in Qum. He said: “My master, absolve me concerning ten thousand dirhams, for I have spent them.” So he said to him: “You are absolved.”

Then when Ṣāliḥ left, Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “One of them pounces upon the wealth of the family of Muḥammad, and their orphans, their needy ones, their poor, and their stranded travelers, and takes it; then he comes and says: ‘Absolve me.’ Do you think he supposed that I would say: ‘I will not do so’? By Allah, Allah will surely question them about that on the Day of Resurrection with an intense questioning.”

So the proper way of reconciling these narrations is what our Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, used to maintain: that whatever has been reported of concession regarding taking khums and disposing of it was reported only in the matter of marriages specifically, due to the reason previously mentioned in the reports from the Imams عليهم السلام, so that the births of their Shiʿah may be wholesome; and it was not reported concerning wealth. And whatever has been reported of strictness regarding khums and exclusive authority over it, then it pertains to wealth. And that which indicates this meaning...

key_terms.أَمْوَالِ: properties or financial assets subject to rightful ownership
key_terms.الْخُمُسِ: the one-fifth tax designated for specific entitled recipients in Shia law
key_terms.الْمَنَاكِحِ: matters of marriage, specifically cited as an exceptional case
key_terms.الْوَقْفَ: the endowment or charitable trust being administered
key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: silver currency units; here, a specified monetary amount
key_terms.فِي حِلٍّ: released from liability or absolved of claim
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection when people will be held to account

ai.seo_question: Did the Imams عليهم السلام permit their Shiʿah to use khums freely during the ghaybah (occultation)?
ai.summary: This report describes a man seeking absolution from Imam Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام after spending funds connected to the rights of Āl Muḥammad. The Imam عليه السلام outwardly absolves him, yet afterward warns of severe divine questioning for usurping such wealth. The compiler then explains that reports permitting disposal of khums apply specifically to marriage-related cases, not to financial property in general.
